newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai citizens invest more in securities.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai citizens invest more in securities.

text.p: Shanghai citizens are investing more of their cash in securities rather than bank deposits due to the abolition of anti-inflation subsidies on deposits and the fall in interest rates, the Liberation Daily said on Tuesday.
In the first nine months, total turnover on Shanghai's securities market hit 1.6 trillion yuan, four times the 1995 total of 400 billion, the paper said.
Bank deposits also rose, but at a slower pace.
Bank deposits in the first quarter grew at a rate of 6.4 billion yuan a month, but by the third quarter had fallen to 2.8 billion per month, the newspaper said.
The central bank abolished the subsidy on April 1 and cut bank loan and deposit interest rates in May and August.
In the first nine months of this year, inflation fell to a year-on-year 6.6 percent against a year-on-year 14.8 percent a year earlier, official figures show.
